Locations: Level 0, the Lobby. Endless yellow rooms, damp carpet, the hum that never stops. Smilers in the dark parts, things that walk behind walls. People noclip in here from the real world and most never leave it. The way down to Level 1 is somewhere past the red zones.

Level 1, the Habitable Zone. Concrete car-park halls, fog, crates of supplies that appear from nowhere, lights that go out. M.E.G. keeps a camp here. Hounds hunt in packs and skin-stealers wear faces. Almond water is the currency of trust.
Level 2, Pipe Dreams. Hot, cramped utility halls full of pipes, steam and oil. The Survivor camp holds a few rooms. Doors open on odd rooms nobody built. The way to Level 3 is through the hot end.

Level 3, the Electrical Station. Brick halls and crawlways, humming machines, sparks, dead ends. Hostile and fast. M.E.G. Base Gamma is reachable from here. Lifts go up to Levels 4 and 5 if you know which.
M.E.G. Base Gamma. The biggest safe settlement anyone knows: a security hall, a mall, a fake little town. Order, rations, guards, rules. The Database terminal is locked to agents.
Level 4, the Abandoned Office. Empty cubicles, water fountains that run with almond water, phones that ring for no one. Quiet and mostly safe. Base Omega sits here. The stairs go down to the hotel.

Level 5, the Terror Hotel. A 1930s grand hotel that never ends: the Main Hall, the Beverly Room ballroom where the polonaise always plays, the Boiler Room's heat. Housekeeping, the Homely Hotel staff and The Originals run it. Some staff are facelings wearing a smile. Samantha the cat wants good meat. Never stay in the Boiler Room alone.

Level 6, Lights Out. Pitch-black concrete labyrinth where flashlights die and only night-vision goggles work. Whispers mimic voices in the dark, walls shift when unwatched, and the concrete stairs descend to the flooded room of Level 7.

Level 7, Thalassophobia. A vast freezing ocean under an endless concrete ceiling. Wanderers arrive through the flooded Entrance Room (the Floating House) atop a basalt rock, with a wooden pier and rowboats leading out to M.E.G. Outpost Seawatch on the near island and Fort Surrender on the far island. Beneath the Daylight, Twilight and Midnight zones prowl two gargantuan leviathans: Entity 20 ('The Thing on Level 7') and 'Tiny'. The abyssal seafloor is carpeted in tar and bones, where underwater tar caves lead down to Level 8.
Level 8, the Cave Systems: the first level wholly enclosed, cold wet karst caves, stalactites, tunnels branchi

Level 8, the Cave Systems: the first level wholly enclosed, cold wet karst caves, stalactites, tunnels branching every way. Most come in wading out of the entrance lake from Level 7's diving bell. The 9th Road is the one marked way through: M.E.G. paint, B.N.T.G. light guides, a Harmouth Speleological Society survey nobody finished. Along it: a flooding cavern where a caver in an orange suit drowned, Hyperspace Lane where the fungus glows and the walls resonate, a nest of man-sized spiders and their broodmother, a boiling tar pit with a B.N.T.G. dredge winch and hands that reach out of it, the 9th Road camp round its fire, and the old asphalt road that runs on toward Level 9. The Lightless haunt two dens off the road: wanderers who lost their lights, stopped wanting them, and now kill anyone who carries one. Nobody knows who laid the asphalt.
Endless overcast wheat and barley fields; no hostile entities; worms below 1 m of soil.

An expansive pasture of wheat and barley stretching in all directions, split into plots by lines of trees and shrubs that never outgrow each other. The sky is always overcast and leaden, with brief light rain and fog and no day or night. Lakes sit below one consistent elevation; the water is clear, safe and tastes earthy. Small sheds, barns and stables stand empty except for wood and nails. Dirt roads with two tire tracks and a grass strip never regrow and often lead to Level 11. Small worms live under one meter of soil; digging deeper makes them surge out and try to burrow into skin. The M.E.G. uses the level as a transit stop and has stopped harvesting its wheat over nutrition worries. Entrances: Level 9 grass walkways, a back road off certain Level 11 streets, an arcade machine on Level 25. Exits: follow a road to Level 11, step into a canola patch for Level 184, swim into a lake for aquatic levels.
An endless, safe city; a hub of trade and settlement.

An endless city of streets, shops, apartments and towers under a warm hazy sky. One of the safest and most settled levels: wanderers live and trade here, and the B.N.T.G. and M.E.G. both keep a presence. Roads out of the city can lead back into the fields of Level 10.

Fort Surrender: a haphazard shelter of broken furniture held together with tar on the nearest island to Level 7's entrance. A handful of survivors, four to nine, who worship The Thing on Level 7 and are rumoured to be hostile to outsiders.
The Lightless
The Lightless: wanderers the cave dark got into
The Lightless: wanderers the cave dark got into. They smash every flashlight they find, sing to the walls, and kill anyone carrying light. Nobody comes back from talking to them.

The 9th Road camp: a fire in the cave kept by M.E.G. operatives, B.N.T.G. traders and a Harmouth caver, the only safe ground between the tar and Level 9.
B.N.T.G.
The Backrooms Nonaligned Trade Group: neutral traders, warehouses, real estate.

The Backrooms Nonaligned Trade Group. Runs warehouses and trade and stays neutral toward nearly everyone. Split from the M.E.G. at Base Gamma; its base Storage Unit on Level 3 is its most important. In this game the B.N.T.G. also sells property, such as the green house on Level 11.
Items: The Backrooms staple drink: restores sanity and thirst.
A clear, slightly sweet water with an almond taste found throughout the Backrooms. It quenches thirst and steadies the mind, and it is the common currency of goodwill between wanderers.
